TITLE: Photosynthesis, Piece by Piece
A: Welcome back to the show. Today we're talking about photosynthesis, and we'll take it in small pieces.
B: Good. First piece only. Listener, before we say it, try to recall in your own words what photosynthesis is.
A: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to make their own food. That's the takeaway: plants make their own food.
B: Okay. So what goes into that process? One ingredient at a time, please.
A: A plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air through tiny openings in its leaves. Takeaway: one ingredient comes in from the air.
B: And the other ingredient?
A: A plant also takes in water from the soil through its roots. Takeaway: water comes up from the soil.
B: Two ingredients in. Now where does the energy come from?
A: Using light energy from the sun, the plant turns carbon dioxide and water into glucose, a kind of sugar. Takeaway: light energy in, sugar out.
B: So glucose is the point of the whole thing?
A: The glucose is the plant's food, and the plant uses it to grow and to store energy. Takeaway: glucose is the plant's food.
A: Nice. Next piece: where does all this happen?
B: Listener, say it before we do. Where does photosynthesis mainly happen?
A: Photosynthesis happens mainly in the leaves. Takeaway: the leaves are the main place it happens.
B: Let's hold one picture in mind for this. A leaf cell is a small room, and inside it sit little green machines.
A: Inside the cells of a leaf are small green structures called chloroplasts. Takeaway: the green structures sit inside leaf cells.
B: And what's inside those green structures?
A: They contain a green pigment called chlorophyll. Takeaway: chlorophyll is the green pigment inside them.
B: Listener, in your own words, what is the green pigment inside chloroplasts called? Say it before A does.
A: It's chlorophyll. Now here's what it does. Chlorophyll absorbs light energy from the sun, mostly red and blue light, and reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.
B: So takeaway: the green light is the part that bounces off, and that's why we see green.
A: And that pigment really matters. Without chlorophyll the plant could not capture the light energy it needs. Takeaway: no chlorophyll means no captured light.
A: Next piece: something leaves the plant. Oxygen is released as a by-product of photosynthesis. Takeaway: oxygen comes out as a by-product.
B: Where does that oxygen go?
A: The oxygen leaves the plant through the same tiny openings in the leaves. Takeaway: out the same openings it came in by.
A: Animals and people breathe in this oxygen, which is one reason plants matter so much to life on Earth.
B: Listener, try to say the word equation before A does. Take your time.
A: The whole process can be written as a word equation: carbon dioxide plus water, using light energy, makes glucose plus oxygen.
[CHECK-IN QUESTION]
A: Last piece: what happens when a plant gets too little of something? A plant that gets too little light, too little water or too little carbon dioxide makes less glucose and grows more slowly. Takeaway: less of the inputs means less glucose.
B: Is that the plant in the dark cupboard?
A: Yes. This is why a plant kept in a dark cupboard turns pale and weak.
A: So to recap: carbon dioxide plus water, using light energy, makes glucose plus oxygen, mainly in the leaves.
